faqs.a: The first full day you stayed sober. If you quit at noon on 1 January, most people count 2 January as day one - but the convention that matters is the one your program uses. Pick it and stay consistent.
faqs.q: What counts as my sobriety date?

faqs.a: Traditionally yes - the counter tracks continuous sobriety. But a slip does not erase your progress or your worth. Many people come back stronger. If you are struggling, contact a support group or helpline.
Because addiction had a price tag, and seeing the number grow reframes every craving as cash kept. It is one of the most motivating numbers in early recovery.
24 hours, 1 week, 30/60/90 days, 6 months, 1 year, then each year. Programs often give chips or coins at these marks.
Research on self-monitoring says yes - visible streaks strengthen commitment. It works best combined with real support: meetings, therapy, or a sponsor.
Screenshot it and share anywhere. Nothing here leaves your device, so your date stays private until you choose to share it.

sobriety-calculator.formula:
Days sober = today - quit date (in days)
Weeks = days / 7
Months = days / 30.44
Years = days / 365.25
Money saved = days x daily spend

Example: quit 1 Jan 2025, today 18 Oct 2026
Days = 655; weeks = 655 / 7 = 93.6
Money at 200/day = 655 x 200 = 131,000
howTo: Enter your quit date (the first day you stayed sober).
Optionally enter what you spent per day - the savings add up fast.
Your days, weeks, months, and years appear instantly.
Watch milestones flip from upcoming to reached.
Screenshot your milestones on big days - you earned them.
keyFacts: Sobriety date = the first full day without the substance.
Common milestones: 24 hours, 1 week, 30 days, 90 days, 6 months, 1 year, then yearly.
Tracking days is a core tool in AA, NA, and SMART Recovery programs.
Money saved is a powerful motivator: daily spend x days sober.
Cravings peak early and fade: most people report far fewer after 90 days.
One day at a time is not a slogan - it is the only unit that ever needs managing.

limitations: A counter supports recovery; it is not treatment.
Dates depend on honest input - the tool cannot verify.
Money saved ignores inflation and interest - it is motivational, not financial advice.
If you relapse, the date resets. That is normal - most recoveries include slips. Reach out for help.

sobriety-calculator.quickAnswer: Enter your quit date and this counter does the rest. Quit on 1 January 2025 and by 18 October 2026 you are 655 days sober - 93.6 weeks, about 1.8 years. At 200 a day, that is 131,000 kept in your pocket. Milestones like 100 days and 1 year mark themselves automatically.

sobriety-calculator.workedExample:
Quit date 1 January 2025, checked 18 October 2026, spent 200/day:
1. Days between: 365 (all of 2025) + 290 (Jan 1 to Oct 18 2026) = 655 days.
2. Weeks: 655 / 7 = 93.6.
3. Years: 655 / 365.25 = 1.79.
4. Money saved: 655 x 200 = 131,000.
5. Milestones reached: 1 week, 1 month, 100 days, 1 year. Next: 1000 days (345 to go).
